metadata.case_name: Baltics vs. Central Asia (institutions vs. resources)
metadata.author: transcribed from live/runs by expansion agent
metadata.key_test: Institutions (P1) dominate resource endowment (P4). Four-way P1 ordinal Estonia>Latvia>Kazakhstan>Uzbekistan holds across gaps far wider than the WGI margin of error (~0.15-0.20), so Mod4 does NOT defer. Resource-poor Baltics outperform resource-rich Central Asia on every dimension.
metadata.notes: WGI Rule of Law figures are on the native -2.5/+2.5 scale (NOT the 0-100 .SC vintage used in case21/Venezuela). 2024 endpoints Latvia 1.09, Kazakhstan -0.38, Uzbekistan -0.66 are high-confidence verbatim; Estonia ~1.2 is approximate (P1 normalized 0.865 given). Safeguard E 30%-of-GDP rentier gate (Mod2) checked year-by-year: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan are intermittent, not structural, rentiers (resemble Nigeria, not Saudi Arabia). Safeguard I (porosity-with-backstop) realized via EU/NATO membership for the Baltics. LIVE strictly more refined than STATIC; both reach the same ordinal.

pre_event.event_description: Post-Soviet institutional divergence: resource-poor Baltics choosing the EU/NATO path vs. resource-rich Central Asian states remaining in Russia's orbit.

context.neighbor_details: Russia = predatory power (Safeguard D); Baltics responded via porosity INTO EU/NATO.
context.backstop_details: EU member (2004) + NATO; the acquis, courts and rule-of-law mechanisms = porosity-with-backstop (Safeguard I, Mod10).

data_gaps: rule_of_law (WGI RoL 2024 ~1.2 approx, -2.5/+2.5 scale; P1 normalized 0.865 given)
Estonia.notes: Highest P1 of the four (P1 normalized 0.865 given). WGI RoL 1996 ~0.3. EU/NATO member since 2004. Resource-poor yet top on every modernization dimension.

context.neighbor_details: Russia = predatory power (Safeguard D); chose porosity INTO EU/NATO.

data_gaps: education_index / life_expectancy_index (HDI 0.879 2022 given; not template fields)
Latvia.notes: rule_of_law = WGI Rule of Law 2024 verbatim 1.09 on the -2.5/+2.5 scale (high-confidence endpoint). WGI RoL 1996 = 0.06. P1 normalized ~0.80 (estimate). Latvia-Kazakhstan gap ~1.47 WGI points >> WGI margin of error, so Mod4 does not defer.

context.neighbor_details: Russia's orbit; CSTO troops deployed into Kazakhstan in January 2022.
context.growth_trajectory: high GDP growth on oil wealth (~$13,340 nominal GDP/capita 2024) atop floor-P1 (Safeguard C reversal risk)

data_gaps: education_index / life_expectancy_index (HDI 0.802 2022 given; not template fields)
Kazakhstan.notes: rule_of_law = WGI Rule of Law 2024 verbatim -0.38 (-2.5/+2.5 scale; its all-time max was -0.37 in 2018; 1996 = -1.42). P1 normalized ~0.34 (estimate). resource_rents_pct_gdp = 2021 value 26.84%; peaks 32.4% (2005) and 33.25% (2008) crossed the Safeguard E 30% gate only in peak-oil years -> intermittent, not structural, rentier (Mod2 does not mechanically trigger inversion). Oil wealth bought GDP/capita but not institutional quality, resilience, or freedom from violence (Bloody January 2022: 238 dead, ~4,500 injured, ~10,000 detained, CSTO intervention).

context.neighbor_details: Russia's orbit; Central Asian authoritarian bloc.
context.growth_trajectory: lowest of the four on every dimension; managed succession Karimov->Mirziyoyev 2016

data_gaps: education_index / life_expectancy_index (HDI 0.727 2022 given; not template fields)
Uzbekistan.notes: rule_of_law = WGI Rule of Law 2024 verbatim -0.66 (-2.5/+2.5 scale; 1996 ~-1.1, series avg -1.08). P1 normalized ~0.29 (estimate, lowest). cpi 2024 = 32. resource_rents_pct_gdp = 2021 value 20.47%; peaks 38.0% (2006) and 30.1% (2008) -> intermittent rentier (Safeguard E gate crossed only in peak years). Lowest on every modernization dimension.

b_violence.agency_note: Mod8: this predicts RISK, not AGENCY

c_convergence.basis: Wide cross-pair P1 gaps vs. narrow within-pair gaps.
c_convergence.falsification_condition: Pairs converge or within-pair members diverge sharply.

d_failure_dimension.prediction: Baltics succeed on P1 (institutions); Kazakhstan's resource wealth does NOT compensate for institutional weakness; Uzbekistan lowest on all dimensions. Institutions dominate resources (P1 > P4) - the framework's central claim.
d_failure_dimension.note: Most exposed to post-hoc coding bias; here it is the cleanest result of the run.
d_failure_dimension.falsification_condition: Resource endowment compensates for institutional weakness anywhere.

result_coding_reference.CONFIRMED: Prediction matched outcome on the specific dimension predicted
result_coding_reference.PARTIALLY_CONFIRMED: Direction correct but magnitude, form, or timing significantly different
result_coding_reference.NOT_APPLICABLE: Prediction type not relevant to this case
result_coding_reference.coding_rule: When ambiguous between confirmed and partial, code PARTIAL. When ambiguous between partial and falsified, code PARTIAL but note ambiguity.

analysis.overall_assessment: Cleanest result of Run 5: 5/5 applicable predictions CONFIRMED. The P1>P4 showdown is decisive - resource endowment did not compensate for institutional weakness anywhere. LIVE more defensible (Mod2 30% gate correctly declines to classify Kazakhstan/Uzbekistan as locked rentiers; adds Safeguard I/H structure); STATIC reaches the same ordinal.
safeguards_triggered: H (centripetal ossification, both Central Asian states)
analysis.what_this_case_uniquely_reveals: Institutional choice dominates resource endowment: resource-poor Baltics that chose EU/NATO porosity-with-backstop vastly outperform resource-rich Central Asian states locked in Russia's orbit. Safeguard E's 30% gate is vindicated as a discriminator (intermittent vs. structural rentiers).
analysis.baseline_impact: None; confirms existing framework (P1>P4 dominance, Safeguards C/D/H/I, Mod2 30% gate, Mod4 margin gating).
